original: so i'm thinking of a better method to improve my speaking English so what i thought is to record，no not to record to review the chat history of today day by day to see the sentence or the expressions i did wrong and i will copy and paste it into a notebook so then i will check and Review and recite maybe to get familiar with them，so i can use them into daily life
better: I'm going to review our chat history daily, copy the incorrect expressions into a notebook, and then study and recite them to use in daily life.
notes: Using 'day by day' is okay, but 'daily' is more concise for frequency. 'Recite' implies memorization, which is a good strategy for fixed expressions (chunks). Note that we 'use something *in* daily life' rather than *into*.
culture: In English-speaking cultures, the concept of 'spaced repetition' (SRS) is often mentioned alongside language learning. Reviewing chat history is a practical application of this!

original: but i think i will stick to the first method just study and learn the chat history between us and when i get enough of... This practice i think it should better and other method i will try later maybe after three months of practicing with you.
better: I'll focus on studying our chat history for now. Once I feel more confident with this method, perhaps after three months, I'll try other ways like finding a conversation partner or watching more English language shows.
notes: 'Stick to' is a great phrasal verb! To sound more natural when talking about progress, 'Once I feel more confident' is better than 'when i get enough of'.
culture: The phrase 'stick to' conveys determination. In Western self-improvement culture, 'consistency' (consistency is key) is highly valued over intensity.

original: I'm not sure but it depends on how much we are chatting each day so i maybe i will start with five minutes chatting with you then i will review the history and to study recite the correct sentences.
better: I'll start with spending five minutes a day reviewing our chat history, and as we chat more, I'll adjust the review time accordingly.
notes: 'Adjust accordingly' is a very useful colocation. It means to change something based on the circumstances. It makes your English sound much more professional.
culture: Small talk about time management and efficiency is common in English. 'Five minutes' is often used as a symbolic start to a habit (The 5-minute rule).

original: Yes，i think so i will do when i think it's needed or necessary and i will review the know book to get improved.
better: I'll take additional notes when necessary and also review my notebook regularly to improve my English.
notes: 'Notebook' is one word. 'Get improved' is slightly passive/unnatural; 'improve my English' (active) is the standard way to express this.
culture: The term 'journaling' is a big trend in English-speaking countries for both mental health and learning. Your notebook is essentially your 'Learning Journal'.

original: so the test method is very thin simple，just speaking with you and practice it every day when i can feel that i'm improved maybe someday so yeah it's clear in my mind i can express correctly and smoothly and fluently don't need too mu- too much time to think of the words or the expressions i to of my idea what i want to express so that's the result i want like native English speaking people.
better: I'll test my progress by speaking with you every day. When I can express myself correctly, fluently, and without thinking too much about the words like a native English speaker, that's when I'll know I've made good progress.
notes: 'Thin simple' isn't a standard phrase; 'very simple' or 'straightforward' is better. 'Thinking on my feet' is an idiom you might like—it means being able to think and speak quickly.
culture: The 'Native Speaker Standard' is a debated topic in linguistics. Nowadays, 'English as a Lingua Franca' (ELF) focuses more on clarity and mutual understanding than sounding exactly like a native.

original: Yes，i think i if i want to ex- express more i have to input more so i can output more and in the meanwhile i will need to read more books and so i can improve my knowledge and the ideas so they are as mentioned they are the contents... So i can input then output，so it will improve my speaking the level.
better: I believe that to express more, I need to input more by reading books and learning new knowledge. This will also give me more ideas to output and improve my speaking level.
notes: 'In the meanwhile' is usually used for two things happening at the same time. Here, 'at the same time' or 'also' fits better. 'Speaking level' is more natural than 'speaking the level'.
culture: The 'Input/Output' model is the foundation of Second Language Acquisition (SLA) theory. You are following a very scientific path!

original: Yes，i think i found the key the where the problem is of my problem so the problem is i do not input much enough for my expression so if i read and learn more i can express more.
better: I've realized that the key to my problem is not inputting enough, so by reading and learning more, I can enhance my expression ability.
notes: 'Enhance' is a great 'Level 2' word to replace 'improve'. It sounds more sophisticated.
culture: Self-reflection is a key part of the 'Growth Mindset'—a popular psychological concept in modern education (Carol Dweck).

original: i took a first injection of weight loss medicine，last week or last Thursday and today is the seventh day and i'm going to take a second one。
better: I took my first injection of weight loss medicine last Thursday. Today is the seventh day, so I'm going to take the second one.
notes: Always capitalize 'I'. When recounting a timeline, connecting clauses with 'so' (cause and effect) helps the listener follow your logic. 'Take an injection' is the correct colocation.
culture: Medical privacy is generally respected, but sharing weight loss journeys (especially with GLP-1 medications like Ozempic) has become a common topic in social conversation recently.

original: Not too much but yes i feel stich when i from the third day and i scratch my skin and it's broken.
better: Not really, but I did feel itchy starting from the third day. When I scratched my skin, it broke.
notes: 'Stich' implies a sharp pain or a sewing stitch. The feeling on the skin is 'itchy' (adj) or 'itch' (noun). 'Broken skin' is the standard way to describe skin damaged by scratching.
culture: Describing symptoms accurately is a key survival skill! 'Itchy', 'rash', 'swollen', and 'irritated' are good vocabulary words to group together here.

original: also i found the good side of the injection so it can stop snoring for me in the night，while sleeping.
better: I also found a positive side effect: it stops my snoring at night while I sleep.
notes: 'Good side' is okay, but in a medical context, 'positive side effect' or 'unexpected benefit' sounds more precise. 'Stop snoring for me' -> 'Stops my snoring'.
culture: Snoring (Sleep Apnea) is a serious health condition. Mentioning it 'stops snoring' is a significant observation that a doctor would be very interested in!

original: The sleep time is almost the same as before and i can wait i can wake up earlier than before.
better: My sleep duration is almost the same as before, but I'm able to wake up earlier now.
notes: 'Sleep time' usually means bedtime (e.g., 10 PM). 'Sleep duration' or 'amount of sleep' refers to the length (e.g., 8 hours). Using 'able to' emphasizes your new capability.
culture: Morning routines are often discussed in terms of 'Productivity'. Waking up early without fatigue is considered a sign of good health and high energy.

original: i will just close my eyes and feel the time collapse
better: I just close my eyes and let time pass.
notes: 'Feel the time collapse' is extremely poetic and creative! However, in daily conversation, it might confuse people. 'Let time pass', 'drift', or 'rest my mind' are standard.
culture: Your original phrase sounds like something from a sci-fi movie (like Interstellar)! It's beautiful, but maybe too dramatic for a casual chat about sleeping in.

original: Soon，yes maybe i will do reading books，loudly and to play taiji boxing
better: Soon, yes. Maybe I'll read books aloud and practice Tai Chi.
notes: 'Read books loudly' -> 'Read aloud'. 'Play Taiji boxing' -> 'Practice Tai Chi'. We 'play' ball games, but we 'do' or 'practice' martial arts and yoga.
culture: Tai Chi (Taiji) is widely respected in the West as a form of 'meditation in motion'. Describing it as 'practicing Tai Chi' connects it to mindfulness routines.

original: maybe the general idea is love too much will cause over lost
better: The general idea is that excessive love leads to great cost.
notes: Translating ancient wisdom is hard! 'Over lost' isn't standard English. 'Great cost', 'Heavy price', or 'Great loss' captures the meaning of '大费' better.
culture: The Dao De Jing is one of the most translated books in the world. This specific concept (Chapter 44) is often discussed in minimalism and stoicism circles in the West.

original: i swam for thirty minutes and i it broke my historical record it went below twenty seven se- minutes so it's twenty six minutes and fifty eight seconds it's the new record of my swimming speed
better: I swam for thirty minutes and broke my personal record. My time went below twenty-seven minutes—26:58 to be exact. That's my new personal best.
notes: 'Historical record' is usually reserved for major events (like the Olympics). For personal fitness, use 'personal record (PR)' or 'personal best (PB)'.
culture: In fitness culture, achieving a 'PR' (Personal Record) is a major milestone. Sharing these wins is a common way to build community with other gym-goers.

original: i can feel my belly muscle hurt because of the belly training yesterday
better: My abs are sore from yesterday's core training.
notes: 'Belly muscle' sounds a bit childish; 'abs' (abdominals) or 'core' is the standard term. 'Hurt' is general, but 'sore' is the specific word for muscle pain after exercise (DOMS).
culture: DOMS (Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness) is often worn as a badge of honor in the West. The saying 'No pain, no gain' is the classic motto here.

original: i use the German cli to create a web page to record the history of our chatting
better: I used the Gemini CLI to create a web page that records our chat history.
notes: Be careful with pronunciation/spelling: 'Gemini' (JEM-in-eye) is the model name, not 'German'. CLI stands for Command Line Interface.
culture: Building your own tools to solve personal problems is the essence of 'Hacker Culture'. You are acting like a true developer!

original: she also congratulated for me
better: She was happy for me. / She congratulated me.
notes: 'Congratulate' takes a direct object ('me'), not 'for me'. However, in this casual context between spouses, 'She was happy for me' sounds warmer and more natural.
culture: Supportive partners are often called 'cheerleaders' in a relationship context. Sharing small wins is crucial for a healthy bond.

original: try more hard to get a better record such like twenty minutes
better: I'll try harder to achieve a better time, like twenty minutes.
notes: 'More hard' -> 'Harder' (comparative adjective). 'Such like' is Chinglish; use 'like' or 'such as'. 'Get a record' -> 'Achieve a time' or 'Break a record'.
culture: Setting specific, measurable goals (like '20 minutes') is part of the 'SMART goals' framework, widely used in Western productivity and fitness.

original: thank you for the introduction of these places and foods we but we have already have our own plan
better: Thanks for the recommendations, but we already have our own plans.
notes: 'Introduction' is too formal for travel tips; use 'recommendations' or 'suggestions'. 'We have already have' is a repetition error; just 'we already have'.
culture: Travel styles vary: some people are 'planners' (itinerary-based) and others are 'spontaneous' (go with the flow). You seem to be a planner!

original: Yes，it's starts on eleven
better: Yes, it leaves at eleven.
notes: For transportation (trains, planes), we say 'leaves' or 'departs'. 'Starts' is for events (movies, meetings). Use 'at' for specific times, not 'on'.
culture: Punctuality is generally valued in travel contexts. 'Leaving at eleven' implies the train moves at that exact minute.

original: First，we'll we are going to have a lunch there
better: First, we're going to have lunch there.
notes: We 'have lunch' (no article 'a'). 'Have a lunch' might imply a specific packed lunch box, but usually, it's uncountable as a meal event.
culture: 'Lunch' is often a lighter meal in English-speaking countries compared to dinner, but on a trip, it's often a major social event.

original: Hello good morning So there are three parts for today's interview And first one is your self introduction Second I will share Our workflow with you Third is the question and answer So let's begin with your self-instruction
better: Good morning. The interview will have three parts: first, your self-introduction; second, I'll explain our workflow; and third, a Q&A session. Let's start with your self-introduction.
notes: As an interviewer, structure is key. 'There are three parts...' is okay, but 'The interview will have three parts' is more direct. 'Self-instruction' means teaching yourself; you meant 'self-introduction'.
culture: Setting the agenda (Agenda Setting) at the beginning of a meeting or interview is a hallmark of professional business communication in the West.

original: Do you speak English every day or sometimes?
better: Do you speak English on a daily basis, or just occasionally?
notes: 'Every day or sometimes' is grammatically correct but simple. 'On a daily basis' sounds more professional. Assessing language frequency is standard for bilingual roles.
culture: In global business, 'working proficiency' is different from 'academic proficiency'. You are correctly probing for their *actual* usage habit.

original: And how much time do you Speak English on yourself. Not at the class duration.
better: And how much time do you spend speaking English by yourself, outside of class?
notes: 'Speak English on yourself' is Chinglish. It should be 'by yourself' or 'on your own'. 'Not at the class duration' -> 'Outside of class hours'.
culture: Self-study (Autodidacticism) is highly valued in employers because it shows initiative and discipline.

original: OK, I need, I think you need to practice more and more.Yes. Yeah, when you do our job, I think it's will be little bit hard for you... But no worry, we will train you before you start the work.
better: I think you'll need to practice more. This role might be challenging because our clients are native speakers. But don't worry, we'll provide training before you start.
notes: 'Practice more and more' sounds a bit like a lecture. Direct feedback ('This role might be challenging') followed by reassurance ('But don't worry') is the 'sandwich method' of feedback.
culture: Managing expectations is crucial in interviews. You honestly flagged the difficulty (native speakers) but immediately offered a solution (training), which is good leadership.

original: which we are looking for advertise accounts. and we will use these accounts to buy traffic from these traffic companies. To promote our products. So this is the workflow of our side, and your job is to get the advertise account open.
better: ...from companies where we're looking to open advertising accounts. We use them to buy traffic and promote our products. Your main task is to get these accounts opened.
notes: 'Advertise accounts' -> 'Advertising accounts' or 'Ad accounts'. 'Get the account open' -> 'Get the account opened' (passive participle).
culture: In the ad-tech industry, terms like 'Traffic Buying', 'Media Buying', and 'Ad Accounts' are standard jargon. Accuracy here establishes your expertise.

original: OK, I will repeat it again, and you can try. OK?
better: Let me explain it one more time, and then you can try summarizing it. How does that sound?
notes: 'I will repeat it again' can sound a bit payload. 'Let me explain it one more time' is softer. Asking 'How does that sound?' invites collaboration rather than just compliance.
culture: Patience with non-native speakers is a key soft skill. You handled the candidate's confusion well by offering to repeat the information.

original: Yes you remember very exactly and i woke up on ten o'clock this morning then we took the bullet train for one and a half hours after getting out of the station went to the campus
better: Yes, you remember exactly. I woke up at ten o'clock this morning, then we took the bullet train for an hour and a half. After leaving the station, we went to the campus...
notes: 'Remember very exactly' -> 'remember exactly' or 'have a great memory'. 'On ten o'clock' -> 'at ten o'clock'. 'Bullet train' is correct, also known as 'high-speed train'.
culture: In China, 'bullet train' (G-train/D-train) is the standard term. In Europe, they might say 'high-speed rail'. 1.5 hours is a 'short commute' by modern Chinese standards!

original: where my wife was finished her postgraduate study for three lives three years so we walk around on the campus around one hour
better: ...where my wife completed her postgraduate studies over three years. We walked around the campus for about an hour.
notes: 'Was finished' is passive; active voice 'completed' or 'finished' is better. 'Postgraduate study' or 'Master's degree'. 'Walk around on the campus' -> 'Walked around the campus'.
culture: Visiting one's 'Alma Mater' (母校) is a nostalgic activity. The term 'Alma Mater' comes from Latin for 'nourishing mother'.

original: Yes and also there are some bad memory but now it should better than before but for something still been feeling bad when we recalling it
better: Yes, there are some bad memories too. Things are better now, but recalling them still makes us feel a bit bad.
notes: 'Bad memory' -> 'Bad memories' (plural). 'It should better' -> 'It is better'. 'Recalling it' or 'looking back' are good phrases for nostalgia.
culture: Acknowledgment of 'bittersweet' memories is a sign of emotional maturity. Life isn't just about the good times.

original: Yes of course make money is the final is the ult- ultimate way to get a better life
better: Yes, of course. Making money is the ultimate goal for a better life.
notes: 'Make money' (verb) needs to be a subject here -> 'Making money' (Gerund). 'Ultimate goal' or 'ultimate means' strengthens your point.
culture: The pursuit of 'Financial Freedom' (FIRE movement) is a huge topic globally. Viewing money as a 'tool' for a better life rather than just an end in itself is a healthy perspective.

original: yes，i have designed a tool to find out the buying and selling points of stock market
better: Yes, I designed a tool to identify buy and sell signals in the stock market.
notes: 'Find out' is a bit casual for software design; 'identify', 'detect', or 'calculate' sounds more technical. 'Buying and selling points' -> 'Buy and sell signals' is the standard trading jargon.
culture: You are building a 'Trading Bot' or 'Algorithmic Trading' tool. This is a high-tech intersection of Finance (FinTech) and Computer Science.

better: Yes, I learned AI-assisted visual coding and cloud development. I used it to build the tool, and it actually works—I've already made some profit.

culture: The trend of 'Citizen Developers' (non-coders building apps using AI/No-Code tools) is exploding. You are on the cutting edge of this wave!

better: Since I traveled to Shanghai, I didn't keep up with my exercise routine.

better: I felt exhausted after swimming for 30 minutes. I planned to swim for an hour, but stopped due to fatigue and pain in my knee.

better: There are some issues with the stock temperature tool. I have to fix them as soon as possible, and it's time-consuming, so I don't have enough time for other things today.

better: I'm not sure, but I'll try. I'm using an AI coding tool called Claude Code, but it's being really unreliable today, so it's making me very angry.

better: I think it works for everything, any bad feelings or symptoms.
notes: Corrected 'work' to 'works'. 'Syndrome' is a specific medical term; 'symptoms' is more general and likely what was intended here.

original: The ingredients of the product are come from traditional Chinese herbal。
better: The ingredients of the product come from traditional Chinese herbs.
notes: 'are come from' is incorrect; it should be 'come from'. 'Herbal' is an adjective; 'herbs' is the noun needed here.
culture: Many modern products are based on traditional Chinese medicine (TCM).

original: I'm not sure just use it when you feel uncomfortable it will make you feel comfortable。
better: I'm not sure. I just use it when I feel uncomfortable, and it makes me feel better.
notes: Separated the sentences for clarity. 'makes me feel better' is a more common and natural-sounding phrase than 'makes you feel comfortable' in this context.

original: It's a happy day because i fixed the automation of my stock temperature tool it was successfully uploaded and it was working correctly。
better: It's a happy day because I fixed the automation of my stock temperature tool. It was successfully uploaded and is working correctly.
notes: Capitalize 'I'. 'Stock temperature tool' is a specific term you use. 'Is working' (present continuous) indicates it's currently functional.
culture: "It works!" is the most satisfying phrase for any developer.

original: Yes，i started working on this from yesterday and there were some big problems so i stopped yesterday and take took a rest and i get up this morning then i check and fix it but it still has some problem so i keep trying and get it done finally until this afternoon
better: Yes, I started working on this yesterday. There were some big problems, so I stopped and took a rest. I got up this morning to check and fix it, but it still had some problems, so I kept trying. I finally got it done this afternoon.
notes: Watch your verb tenses (past tense for yesterday: 'took', 'got', 'kept'). 'Until this afternoon' implies the action stopped at that time.
culture: "Debugging" often requires stepping away and coming back with fresh eyes.

original: Yes，it's a very practical and useful strategy for get progress moved forward and i also use this technique in my daily life such as exercise routine so i did three items today one is i was supposed to swim and do rowing machine but i gave up because i have to fix my stock temperature tool first so i do i did the exercise in room i did push，ups and belly training
better: Yes, it's a very practical strategy for making progress. I also use this technique in my daily life, such as in my exercise routine. I did three things today. I was supposed to swim and use the rowing machine, but I skipped them to fix my stock tool first. Instead, I exercised in my room, doing push-ups and core training.
notes: 'Get progress moved forward' -> 'Making progress'. 'Gave up' usually implies quitting permanently; 'skipped' or 'missed' is better for a single session. 'Belly training' -> 'Core training'.
culture: "Prioritization" often means trading one good habit (exercise) for an urgent task (work), which is a common modern dilemma.

original: good evening today，i went to Hong Kong with my wife to get some bank accounts... Opened today，i.
better: Good evening. Today, I went to Hong Kong with my wife to get some bank accounts opened.
notes: 'Get something done' structure (get bank accounts opened). 'Opened' is the past participle describing the state of the accounts.
culture: Hong Kong is a major financial hub, and opening bank accounts there is a common task for cross-border finance.

original: It took around one hour it's very easy and simple just because we are applying online accounts no need to go to the counter，but due to the bad internet access in the time，we took some more time。
better: It took around an hour. It was very easy and simple because we were applying for online accounts, so there was no need to go to the counter. However, due to poor internet access, it took a bit longer.
notes: 'In the time' -> 'At the time' or just omit. 'Bad internet access' -> 'Poor internet connection'. 'We took some more time' -> 'It took a bit longer' (referring to the process).
culture: "Digital Banking" (Virtual Banks) is becoming the norm, reducing the need for physical branches ("counters").

original: No we tried and it succeeded，but with only one account it's not i we cannot get it a applied through we don't know the reason.
better: No, we tried and succeeded, but there's one account we couldn't get approved. We don't know the reason.
notes: 'Get it applied through' -> 'Get approved' or 'Get the application through'. 'It succeeded' -> 'We succeeded' or 'It worked'.
culture: Banking compliance (KYC/AML) can be opaque; sometimes applications are rejected without clear reasons.

original: Sure yes，we did，but the food is not so ideal delicious，so we didn't finish them we just have two thirds。
better: Yes, we did, but the food wasn't that delicious, so we didn't finish it. We only ate about two-thirds.
notes: 'Ideal delicious' is unnatural -> 'That delicious' or 'Very tasty'. Food is uncountable ('finish it', not 'finish them'). 'Have two thirds' -> 'Ate two-thirds'.
culture: Leaving food can be seen as wasteful, but "voting with your fork" is a valid critique of a bad meal.

original: Yes... We got a takeaway.
better: Yes, we got takeaway.
notes: 'A takeaway' (noun) or just 'takeaway' (uncountable concept). In the US, it's 'takeout'.
culture: "Pork Chop Bun" (猪扒包 - Zhūpá bāo) is a famous Macau/Hong Kong snack.

original: good，evening so i'm back from Hong Kong with my wife we went there by bullet train and for six hours and we came back by airplane for two and a half hours
better: Good evening. I'm back from Hong Kong with my wife. We went there by bullet train, which took six hours, and came back by airplane, which took two and a half hours.
notes: Structure travel time with relative clauses ('which took...'). 'Bullet train' is the correct term for high-speed rail.
culture: Comparing travel modes (Speed vs. Comfort) is a common small talk topic.

original: Yes，definitely the space is more more more more more is more larger than the airplane's seat
better: Yes, definitely. The space is much larger than the airplane seats.
notes: Avoid repetition ('more more more'). Use 'much larger' (comparative + intensifier). 'Space' or 'Legroom' is the specific term for seat comfort.
culture: 'Legroom' is the most valued commodity in modern travel.

original: Yes，when i got on the train i was planning to read a book，but after reading about half an hour i feel i felt sleepy and fall asleep for one or two hours again after waking up... i continued to reading the book
better: Yes, when I got on the train, I planned to read a book. But after reading for about half an hour, I felt sleepy and fell asleep for an hour or two. After waking up, I continued reading.
notes: 'Continued reading' (gerund) is standard. 'Fall asleep' -> 'Fell asleep' (past). 'For about half an hour' (duration).
culture: Reading on a train is a classic image of leisure, but 'napping' is often the reality.

original: Ican't remember the book the novel name... it's telling a story about a man whose family was killed by his opponents due to their cre- greedy and anxious maybe generous so he tried to revenge and he was put into the jail by one of his opponents for fourteen years he came back with great fortune who gave him in the jail
better: I can't remember the novel's name, but it's about a man whose family was killed by his rivals out of greed and jealousy. He tried to get revenge but was imprisoned for fourteen years. He returned with a great fortune given to him in jail.
notes: 'Opponents' -> 'Rivals' or 'Enemies'. 'Revenge' is usually a noun ('get revenge' or 'take revenge'), 'avenge' is the verb. 'Greedy and anxious' -> likely 'Greed and Jealousy/Envy'.
culture: This is clearly *The Count of Monte Cristo* (Le Comte de Monte-Cristo). It's the archetype of the 'Revenge Thriller'.

original: Yes，i found this novel is very attractive and i can't stop reading it the plot is so amazing and unpredictable so many zigzags
better: Yes, I found this novel very engaging, and I couldn't stop reading it. The plot is amazing and unpredictable, with so many twists and turns.
notes: 'Attractive' describes people/objects; for books, use 'engaging', 'compelling', or 'gripping'. 'Zigzags' -> 'Twists and turns' is the correct idiom for plot changes.
culture: A 'page-turner' is a book you can't put down.

original: i have just made a new version of temperature tool originated from stock market and i transferred it into Crypto market hopefully，it will work.
better: I have just made a new version of a temperature tool originating from the stock market and transferred it to the Crypto market. Hopefully, it will work.
notes: 'Originated from' -> 'Originating from' (participle phrase). 'Transferred it into' -> 'Transferred it to'.
culture: "Porting" a strategy from one market (Stocks/Equities) to another (Crypto) is a common topic in algorithmic trading.

original: Because i'm not making profit in the Crypto market and i used this stock market tool To make profit，so i want to try.
better: Because I'm not making a profit in the Crypto market, but I use this stock market tool to make a profit, I want to try it.
notes: Avoid 'Because... so...'. 'Make profit' -> 'Make a profit'.
culture: "Arbitrage" implies profiting from price differences, but here it's about arbitraging *logic* or *strategies* across markets.

original: I think it will take around at least one month because this stock market temperature need took around half a year.
better: I think it will take at least one month because this stock market temperature tool took around half a year.
notes: 'Take around at least' is redundant -> 'Take at least'. 'Need took' is a tense conflict -> 'Took'.
culture: Software development timelines often suffer from the "Planning Fallacy" (underestimating time), but comparing to past projects is a good estimation technique.

original: So this tool was supposed to detect the buying and selling signals so i will trace back when it detects the signals and i will buy or sell with the signal then i can see if it works.
better: This tool is supposed to detect buying and selling signals. I will check back when it detects the signals, buy or sell based on them, and then see if it works.
notes: 'Trace back' usually means finding the origin. 'Check back' or 'Monitor' is better here. 'Buy or sell with the signal' -> 'Buy or sell based on the signal'.
culture: "Paper Trading" (simulated trading) vs. "Backtesting" (testing on past data) vs. "Live Trading" (real money).

original: No i didn't design this function to s- s- it cannot test back.
better: No, I didn't design this function, so it can't backtest.
notes: 'Test back' -> 'Backtest' (specific industry term).
culture: Backtesting is considered essential in Quant trading to verify a strategy before risking capital.

original: The buy in signal so i can buy in then waiting for the selling signal so i can sell it out then i can make a profit.
better: The buy-in signal, so I can buy in, then wait for the selling signal to sell out and make a profit.
notes: Tense consistency: 'can buy... then wait' (not 'waiting'). 'Sell it out' is okay, often just 'sell' or 'exit the position'.
culture: "Buy low, sell high" is the mantra, but "execution" is where the difficulty lies.

original: Yes，i have eleven cryptos bought in the past and they are losing money so i want to save them back and i make a profit in the future.
better: Yes, I have eleven cryptos I bought in the past. They are losing money, so I want to recover my losses and make a profit in the future.
notes: 'Save them back' -> 'Recover my losses' or 'Turn them around'.
culture: "Bag holding" is the slang for holding losing positions hoping they will recover.

original: First i will use the tool to help with the all the eleven and then we'll start a new one maybe it's better to do them at the same time.
better: First, I will use the tool to help with all eleven, then start with new ones. Maybe it's better to do them at the same time.
notes: 'The all the eleven' -> 'All eleven'.
culture: "Diversification" vs. "Concentration".
